BadRequest.description: Bad request, or a query parameter that is not allowed

Forbidden.description: Wrong Host (unknown_host), an Origin header (origin_refused), a scope the device lacks (forbidden_scope; see each operation's x-ainkrad-scope), or an operation marked x-ainkrad-destructive without a live step-up elevation (step_up_required)

Unauthorized.description: auth_failed (any signature or device failure, alike whatever the reason), clock_skew (with server_time), or session_expired

models.description: A preset: how many model ids the provider listed (E7-3); absent otherwise.

result.description:
`ok`, or why not. A Claude plan: `token_expired`, `limit_reached`, `no_runner` (none that
may hold the token is online), `runner_outdated`, `runner_busy`, `runner_failed`,
`egress_not_proven`, `sandbox_unavailable`, `unreachable`, `timeout` or `failed`. An
API-key account: the key test's class (`ok`, `auth_failed`, ...) or `no_runner`.

runner.description: The runner device that made the check; absent when none was asked.

AccountDetail.description: What an `admin` write answers: the account and the runners its key may be leased to.

chain.description: The chain that holds the pool (set by `createAccount`).

pool.description: The pool the account joined (set by `createAccount`).

runners.description: Runner device ids, explicit (never a wildcard).

AccountHealth.description: An account's health counters, as the scheduler keeps them.

auth_streak.description:
A subscription's failed sessions in a row; the third keeps it out of new runs
(`state_reason` `auth_suspected`) until an admin answers.

fail_streak.description: Upstream errors counted in the current ten-minute window; three put it out for ten minutes.

last_success_at.description: The last time a request or a session on it went well.

plan_limit.description:
A subscription's latest plan-limit snapshot, as its harness last said it (harness output:
it can only cool the account, never disable it).

upstream_class.description: The last status class its gateway reported on any of its sessions.

AccountLogin.description: Where a sign-in has got to. Never a token or a code.

code.description:
The one-time device code to type on that page (`codex-sub`), from `open_url` on. Not a
credential. Absent for a sign-in with no device code. A runner-bound sign-in takes no
`/code`: it goes `open_url` then `storing` then `done` by itself once the user finishes.

expires_at.description: Ten minutes after it began; a sign-in open past it fails.

reason.description: Why it `failed` or was `cancelled`; provider text passes the redactor.

state.description:
`starting`, `open_url` (open `url`, then send the code), `waiting_code` (the code is with
the runner), `storing`, `done` (see `account_id`), `failed` (see `reason`) or `cancelled`.

AccountMeter.description: One row's meter: `fraction` of the most binding limit, in words of `used` of `limit` per `window`.

fraction.description:
Used over the limit, 0 to 1 (1 at or past it), of the most used limit; absent when the
account has no limit and no plan snapshot.

resets_at.description: When that window starts over; absent for `total`.

source.description: Where the number comes from: `plan` (the harness's snapshot) or `budget`.

state.description:
`ready`; `limit_hit` (a limit or quota stops it until `state_until`); or `unavailable`
(cooling after errors, unhealthy or disabled: see the account's `state_reason`).

state_until.description: When a `limit_hit` account is usable again; absent when unknown (a `total` budget).

used.description:
With `limit` and `unit`: `38` of `100` `percent`; `12000000` of `50000000` `usd_micros`;
`60` of `900` `messages`; or `tokens`.

window.description:
`five_hours`, `day`, `week`, `month` or `total`; a plan window the Core does not know keeps
the harness's own name.

allowed.description: Absent switch means allowed: `false` only when someone switched it off.

input_per_mtok_micro.description:
List price per million input tokens, in millionths of a dollar; absent when the model has
no price (it then runs at the flagged default price).

model.description: Exactly as the provider names it.

AccountModels.description: What `GET /accounts/{id}/models` answers: the model ids the provider listed for the account.

fetched_at.description: When the list was read; absent when none was.

items.description:
Every model the account can name with its price and switch: the listed ids, the provider's
priced ones and any switched off. Absent when there is none.

models.description:
Exactly as the provider names them; empty until a list was read (a preset's add or check
through a runner). No price: an unpriced model runs at the flagged default price.

utilization.description: A fraction of the window's limit, past 1 at the limit.

AccountSpend.description: One account's usage. No key, secret name, delivery or runner: it is for a `read` device.

recent_drops.description: Provider drops in the last hour.

AccountTested.description: What `POST /accounts/{id}/test` answers: a status class and a latency, never a response body.

models.description: A preset: how many model ids the provider listed (E7-3); absent otherwise.

result.description:
As [`LastTest::result`], or `inconclusive`: the provider's model list needs no key and its
definition declares no `test_path`, so nothing was sent and nothing is known of the key.

runner.description: The runner device that made the request (empty when `result` is `inconclusive`).

undo_until.description: Only for `deleteAccount`: when its Undo window ends (RFC 3339, UTC).

AgentApproval.description: A Code Mode write the Core holds until a person decides (plan E6).

args.description: The arguments the AI session passed, with secrets redacted and long texts cut.

expires_at.description: After this the call is refused `approval_timeout`.

input.description:
`{summary, args, reason}` as one object, the shape of a harness approval's `input`, so a card
shows it without guessing.

reason.description: Why it needs a person, in a sentence.

risk.description: `risky`: the only class that waits for a person.

AgentApprovals.description: The approvals one session waits on, newest last.

always.description:
With `approved`: also allow this kind of call for every session of the session's project
from now on ("Always for this project"). The Core stores a rule derived from the request
(a safe shell command's first words, or a plain path prefix inside the project folder) and
approves later matching requests itself, auditing each (`agent.approval_auto`). 400
`rule_not_allowed` (nothing is decided) for a tool or command that can only be approved
once, or a session of no project. See `listApprovalRules`.

reply.description: Told to the agent; a denial's reason.

AgentEdit.description:
The `edit` of a file edit's `tool_use` entry (Claude's Edit, MultiEdit, Write and NotebookEdit,
Codex's fileChange, OpenCode's edit, multiedit and write): what each change took out and put
in, the same shape for every harness. The texts are at most 64 KiB in all; past that they are
cut at a line end, `truncated` is set, and the entry's `input` keeps only its small fields.

AgentEditChange.description:
One change of an `AgentEdit`. A new file's `old` is empty, a deleted one's `new`. From a
unified diff (Codex), the lines before and after with the hunk headers left out.

AgentFileRevert.description: A file of a session's folder to put back as it was before the session's edits.

path.description: Inside the session's folder: absolute, or relative to it.

AgentFileWrite.description: A file to write into a session's folder.

content.description: The file's whole new text, at most 256 KiB.

path.description: Inside the session's folder: absolute, or relative to it. Not under `.git`.

AgentFolderListing.description: One level of a session's folder.

dir.description: The folder listed, relative to the session's folder; empty for the folder itself.

entries.description: Directories first, then by name; at most 500.

truncated.description: There were more than the entries shown.

attachments.description:
Files added with `addAgentAttachment` (`at_…`, at most 16): written into the session's
folder on its runner before the message goes, and named at its end by their paths.

text.description: Up to 16 KiB; may be empty when `attachments` names a file.

AgentModeChange.description: A session's new mode: either field, or both.

effort.description:
How hard the harness thinks: `low`, `medium`, `high` or `max`; absent, unchanged. Takes
effect at the next turn (the harness is restarted with it). 400 `effort_unsupported` for a
harness that cannot (`can_set_effort`).

plan.description: Plan mode on or off; absent, unchanged.

AgentSecret.description: A secret for the session: the broker's secret `name`, delivered under `var`.

var.description:
`[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*`, not `PATH`, `HOME` or a loader's: the value (`env` delivery), the
path of a 0600 file holding it (`file`), or of an askpass helper (`askpass`).

AgentSession.description: An agent session: a harness on a runner.

account.description: The account the session holds, whatever its delivery (an API key or a subscription).

agent.description: The opaque agent id the create named (the key of its chain binding).

attempt.description: Which attempt of its run it is, from 0.

can_set_effort.description:
Whether its effort can be set (`effort` on `createAgentSession` or `setAgentSessionMode`):
its harness takes one (Claude, Codex) and its runner relays it.

can_stop_subagents.description:
Whether one sub-agent of it (a running `Task`/`Agent` tool call) can be stopped on its own
with `stopAgentSubagent`: its harness can (Claude Code) and its runner relays it.

chain.description: The chain as it was when the session began (an edit never moves a running run).

chain_id.description:
The chain the run draws its accounts from; absent for a session that names its account
itself or uses the runner's own login.

chain_pos.description: The entry of `chain` the run sits on, from 0.

effort.description:
Its effort level now (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`), from the create or the latest
`setAgentSessionMode`; absent: the harness's own default.

failed_over_to.description: The attempt that replaced this one.

failover_class.description:
Why the run was moved off this attempt (`rate_limited`, `quota`, `auth`, `budget_pool`, …).
An ended run's last attempt says in `outcome.failover` (`{result, why, reasons}`) why it
could not move on. Admin only.

folder.description:
The absolute path of the folder its harness works in, on its runner (`runner`): its
worktree under the runner's work root, or its scratch dir there. Absent until the runner
reports it after the start. A worktree is moved away when its run ends, so an ended
session's folder may no longer exist.

harness_session.description: The harness's own session id, what a resume continues.

live.description: A live conversation (`createAgentSession`'s `live`): the state is `waiting` between answers.

place_reason.description:
Why the Core placed it where it runs (E15): `core`, `overflow` (the Core was full) or
`pinned` (a runner-bound login); absent for a session placed before E15.

placed_on.description: The name of the machine it runs on (`runner` is its id), for "Ran on X".

plan.description: Plan mode: the harness reads and plans, edits nothing (Claude Code's `plan`).

policy.description:
Its permission mode now: `ask`, `accept_edits` or `sandboxed` (the create's `policy.mode`,
or the latest `setAgentSessionMode`).

project_id.description:
The project it was started for (`createAgentSession` with `project_id`): its workspace is
that project's repos, cloned from the Core's copies. Absent for any other session.

repicked.description: How many accounts a launch refused after the pick before the one it holds (at most 2).

resumes.description: How many times it was resumed.

run.description:
The run it belongs to: its first attempt's id. A failover is a new session (an attempt) of
the same run; filter `listAgentSessions` with `run`.

secrets.description: The secrets it is leased at each start, by name.

skip_pools.description: The pools a budget stop took out of the run's chain. Admin only.

state.description:
`starting`, `running` (working), `waiting` (a live session finished its answer and waits
for the user's next message; it still holds its runner slot), `interrupted` (its runner
restarted; it is resumed), `ended`, `lost`.

title.description: A short name: the first message's start, or the one `titleAgentSession` set.

turn_cost_approximate.description:
`turn_cost_usd_micros` is a lower estimate: Claude Code reports an answer's output tokens as
they were when it started, so the turn's own closing `usage` entry is the exact count.

turn_cost_usd_micros.description:
While `running`: what the answer that runs now has cost so far, in micro-dollars, from the
harness's mid-turn token reports (its `usage_so_far` entries) at the price book's rates for
the session's model. 0 when its message has just started it; absent when no answer runs or
the model has no price. It moves with the transcript: each change comes with an
`agent.transcript` event.

upstream_class.description:
The last status class its own gateway reported: `ok`, `rate_limited`, `quota`,
`server_error`, `auth_failed`, …

waiting.description:
Set while a chain session waits for an account: it stays `starting` until `until`, or
until `scheduler.wait_max_secs` ends the run.

workspace.description:
The repo and worktree it works in, as the create sent it (`{"repo", "base", "branch", …}`);
absent for a scratch dir.

AgentTitle.description: A new title for a session.

title.description: At most 60 characters; empty clears it (the list then shows the session's harness).

at_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds, on the runner: when it took the event. A `tool_use`'s is when the call
started (a sub-agent's `Task` or `Agent` included), an `approval_request`'s when the
approval was asked.

body.description:
A harness event, or the session's own (`started`, `message`, `approval_request`,
`approval_decided`, `interrupted`, `gap`, `ended`), redacted. A file edit's `tool_use` also
carries `edit` (`AgentEdit`). A harness that shows its reasoning (Claude Code's `thinking`
blocks) adds `{"type": "thinking", "text": "…"}` entries, before the text or tool call they
belong to, at most 16 KiB each (cut with a `[cut]` marker); the other harnesses send none.
An `approval_decided` the Core made by a project's "always" rule carries `note` saying which.

seq.description: From 1, by one: replay from any `seq` with `after`.

AgentUsage.description: Tokens used, as the harness reported them.

cost_usd_micros.description: Millionths of a US dollar, when the harness says.

AgentWaiting.description: Why a chain session has not started: it waits for an account to come back.

since.description: Its first wait; it waits `scheduler.wait_max_secs` in all.

until.description: When the earliest account may be back.

why.description: A fixed phrase: every account the chain can use is cooling, limited or at its cap.

queued.description: `false` when this key was already used: nothing was queued.

AgentWakeRequest.description: A wake for an idle session.

key.description:
Makes the wake idempotent: asking again with the same key queues nothing (it is kept for
30 days). 1 to 128 of `A-Za-z0-9_.:-`; absent, the Core makes one up.

text.description: The next turn, 1 byte to 16 KiB; absent, the session just continues.

complete.description: False when the budget (or a card's own cap) cut something.

ids.description: The ids of the records in the bundle.

text.description:
The bundle, wrapped once as outside data; empty when there is nothing to add. Every record
line starts with its id in brackets.

compacted.description: The source's text was removed by retention; only the citation remains.

text.description: The source's start of text, inside the outside-text envelope; empty when `compacted`.

truncated.description: The snippet was cut at 2000 characters.

kind.description: Always `record`: a fact in force. Sources are read through `brainAiEvidence` only.

text.description: The match, inside the outside-text envelope.

complete.description:
False when a cap (rooms per search, records per room for meaning) cut what was read, so a
missing hit may exist. Always set; optional in the schema for the same reason as `ranked_by`.

ranked_by.description:
`keyword`, `meaning` or `both`: how these hits were ranked. Always set; optional in the schema
only because it joined the contract after 1.0 (a new field may not be required).

rooms_closed.description: Visible rooms that were closed and so not searched.

AiOrder.description: The default order and the per-agent overrides.

items.description: Empty until the first account is added.

AiPast.description: A record a current one replaced. `text` is outside data, like every record text.

history.description:
Only `brainAiRecord`: what this record replaced, newest first (B4-02), so "what was true in
March" stays answerable. A replaced record is reachable only through its successor in memory.

sources.description: Item ids of the sources it came from.

text.description: Its tags and body, inside the outside-text envelope; a list cuts a long body.

rooms_closed.description: Visible rooms that were closed and so not read.

open.description: Whether the room's lease is live: only an open room can be searched or read.

AiTidy.description: The AI tidy of this run's proposal: what the local model changed by itself.

changes_url.description: The list of changes: `GET` it for "See changes".

state.description:
`applied` (the proposal is tidied), `undone` (restored as it was before; the next re-sort
may tidy again) or `declined`: the AI was not confident. Its tidy would have changed too much
(more than 30% of the items as near-copies, or fewer than a third of the rooms left; `summary`
says how much), so nothing was changed and the proposal is as the rules made it.

ApiVersion.description: The contract a server speaks: `/api/<major>` and its additions so far.

minor.description: Bumped on every additive change within the major.

pattern.description:
What it covers: a shell command's first words (`cargo test`), or a path prefix inside the
project folder (`src/api/`, or one file's relative path).

sas.description: The SAS shown on both screens.

scopes.description: Narrower scopes than the pairing bound; never wider.

archived.description: False when it was archived already.

total.description: Records of the area in the open rooms, before the limit.

seen_at.description: When a source last showed it.

latest.description: The newest record's text, cut short.

today.description: Records added in the last 24 hours.

evidence.description: Sources stored across all rooms (the Evidence area, shown under Explore).

locked_rooms.description: Rooms not read because they are not open.

AuditDay.description: One day of the audit log.

hours.description: Rows per hour of that day, 24 numbers.

kinds.description: Rows per kind (every kind, zero included).

needs_attention.description: Rows that need a look: failures, refusals, lockouts, raised alarms.

entity_id.description: A numeric entity id; absent for a device, which is named by `entity_ref` only.

entity_ref.description: The entity's public id: a device's opaque `d_…` id, else `entity_id` as text.

origin.description: What started it; absent on rows from before origins.

AuditPage.description:
A page of the audit log, newest first. `next_before` continues with older rows, absent on
the last page.

AuditStats.description: The audit log counted, newest day first.

at.description: When the Core accepted the rooms.

rooms.description: The rooms it made that are still active.

BackupFile.description: One backup on the host's disk.

BackupRetention.description: How many local backups the Core keeps.

helper.description: `present` (the host helper answered), `absent` (not installed here) or `error`.

keep.description: The backups kept in the Core's backups folder; older ones are removed after each backup.

BackupRun.description: The newest run of the backup unit, as systemd says.

result.description: `success`, or what systemd calls the failure (`exit-code`, `timeout`…).

running.description: Whether a backup is running now.

request_id.description: The id the start is audited under (`host.backup_requested`, `host.action_result`).

BackupStatus.description: The backup schedule and history of the Core machine.

helper.description: `present` (the host helper answered), `absent` (not installed here) or `error`.

history.description: The backups on disk, newest first, at most 60.

keep.description: How many local backups the Core keeps (`PUT /system/backups/retention` changes it).

next_at.description:
When the timer fires next, in any clock zone of the host (the helper asks systemd for unix
time); absent when the timer is not armed.

items.description: Items as `brain-model`'s JSON Schema describes them.

distilling.description: Distils running now, and queued behind them.

failed.description: Distils and overview writes that failed in the last day.

health.description: `ok`, or `attention` when a distil or an overview failed in the last day.

last_done_at.description: When the last distil finished, if any.

needs.description: What Brain waits on from the person (only ever an AI account, a runner, a local model or the unlock).

state.description: `locked` (no key), `needs_you`, `working` or `idle`. The icon shows this.

context.description: Build context inside that repo; default `.`.

dockerfile.description: Path of the Dockerfile inside that repo; default `Dockerfile`.

BundledAttested.description:
Who may be told apart as "the runner bundled in this Mac's app" (E6, L1): the pairing row of
`runner` after the Mac app, which reads that runner's own enrolment file on its local disk
(a remote runner has none there), attests it.

complete.description: False when the budget cut a record that would have made it.

ids.description: The records on the card, in order.

Chain.description:
An ordered fallback chain of 1 to 16 pools. Deprecated with the pool routes: the AI order (`/api/v1/ai-order`) replaces it. A new session draws an account from the first
entry that has one to give.

is_default.description: The user's default chain serves an agent bound to none.

ChainBinding.description: An agent's binding: its sessions get this chain.

agent.description: The opaque agent id, 1 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`.

ChainEntry.description:
One step of a chain: the pool tried at this position, and the harness and model its accounts
run. The harness is the pool's provider's own.

model.description: The model for that harness; absent, the harness's default.

challenge.description:
32 bytes, base64url (43 characters), opaque to the client; spend it once within
`expires_in` seconds.

options.description:
A passkey device's step-up only: `{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions}`
over `challenge`, for `navigator.credentials.get`.

device_id.description: The device that will answer it, `d_…`.

rows.description: Records the set changed (a purge keeps none).

summary.description: The line the App shows, such as "Saved 5 · reinforced 3 · replaced 1".

undone_at.description: When Undo ran; none while it can still be undone.

more.description: More rows follow: ask again with `after` set to the last `seq`.

after.description: The record as the change left it; none: the change removed it.

before.description: The record as it was (the `records` columns and `_sources`); none: it did not exist.

requested.description:
True when the request was taken. The Core acts on it at its next tick, under its caps;
nothing is distilled in this call.

ClaimBody.description:
A claim. The credential hash is SHA-256 of the canonical typed code (upper-cased, dashes
and spaces dropped, `I`/`L` read as `1` and `O` as `0`: 10 ASCII Crockford characters), or
of the QR secret's 16 decoded bytes (not its base64 text). Vectors:
`crates/server/tests/vectors/pairing-v1.json`.

code.description: The typed code (`ABCDE-FGHJK`, any case); or `secret`.

device_name.description:
What to call this device: 1 to 64 characters of plain text, no control characters. It
becomes the device's name in place of the pairing's (an invite's is `owner`).

pop.description:
The routine key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-PAIR-V1` LF `<core_fp>` LF `<base64url of the credential hash>` LF
`<fp(routine)>` LF `<fp(stepup) or ->`, no trailing newline; fp is base64url SHA-256 of
the SPKI.

pop_stepup.description: The step-up key over the same string, with `stepup_spki`.

routine_spki.description: The routine key: a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url.

stepup_spki.description: The step-up key, where the device has one.

session.description: An AI session that has not started yet.

core_spki.description: The Core identity SPKI, base64url: its fingerprint must equal the QR's `c`.

device_id.description: The new device, `d_…`, pending until approved; for an invite it is active already.

pairing_id.description:
The pairing, `p_…`: with `core_spki` and its own key the device computes the SAS
itself and shows that, rather than trusting `sas` from whoever answered.

sas.description:
Show this; the approver compares it with theirs. The first 16 upper-case Crockford
characters of SHA-256(`AINKRAD-SAS-V1` ‖ core_spki ‖ routine_spki ‖ pairing id as
UTF-8), as `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`. Meaningless for an invite: nothing waits on a match.

ClosestHint.description:
An Unsorted item that no rule placed but that looks like it belongs in a room: "Looks like it
belongs in <room_name> (0.9x)". To accept: when `in_review`, `PATCH /imports/{run}/items` with
`proposal = room_id`; otherwise (a room committed earlier) split Unsorted with `item_ids = [item_id]`
and `name = room_name`. AI suggestions are never accepted automatically, whatever the rules say.

room_id.description: A proposal id of this run when `in_review`, else the id of a room already committed.

score.description: Cosine similarity to the room's centroid, 0 to 1.

CommitKeep.description: The Review's one decision (API minor 73): the rooms to import; every other room is refused.

keep.description:
The proposals to import. Every other open proposal is refused (its items wiped, their hashes
kept so they never come back), Unsorted aside. A room imported already may be named again.

keep_unsorted.description: Unsorted's items wait in "No room yet" (true, the default) or are refused and deleted (false).

held.description: Accepted proposals that wait: employer and client rooms until `room_backup` exists.

created_by.description: `admin` devices: the device that made it.

expires_at.description: When the access token ends, when known.

grant_count.description: `admin` devices: how many grants say who may use it.

identity.description: The account or site the last test read (a GitHub login, an Atlassian account at a site).

is_default.description: The kind's default connection: used when several cover a call.

my_capabilities.description:
Other devices: what the caller may do with it (the capabilities of the grants that name
the caller); never anyone else's grants or limits.

ConnectionApp.description: Ainkrad's OAuth app for a kind, as configured: never a secret.

app_install_configured.description: GitHub: the GitHub App (repositories) is set up.

configured.description: Sign in works for the kind.

redirect_uri.description: Atlassian: the redirect address to register with Atlassian, exactly.

ConnectionAppField.description: One field of an app's config.

secret.description: A secret is write-only: only `set` is ever said.

value.description: The value of a field that is no secret.

ConnectionFlow.description: A sign-in as it stands: poll it.

authorize_url.description: Atlassian: what the Mac app opens in the browser.

error_code.description: When `failed`: a fixed code and a plain sentence with the fix.

identity.description: Once `connected`: who it is connected as.

sites.description: Atlassian, `choose_site`: the sites to pick from.

state.description: Atlassian: the `state` the redirect must carry; hand it back with the `code`.

user_code.description: GitHub: the code to type, large.

ConnectionFlowCallback.description: What the Mac app's loopback listener received. No `Debug`.

id.description: The Atlassian cloud id: what `chooseConnectionSite` takes.

ConnectionGrant.description: What someone may do with a connection.

limits.description: The resources it reaches, by the kind's limit key; none: any.

ConnectionKind.description: What a screen draws a kind's setup from.

configured.description: Whether Sign in works: Ainkrad's app for the kind is set up on this Core.

install_url.description: GitHub: where the person installs the GitHub App to choose repositories, when it is set up.

ConnectionResource.description: One thing on a connection a grant's limit can name, for the picker (step "Which repositories").

elevated_until.description: Until when this session may call routes marked `x-ainkrad-destructive`.

unlocked_until.description:
For an app unlock (`purpose: session`, and the heartbeat): until when it holds if no

EntryOrigin.description:
What started an audited change, and the root of its chain. Absent on rows from before
origins (unknown).

reference.description: The device (`d_…`), job (`owner/job`) or session (`as_…`) it names, when there is one.

root_kind.description: The kind of the first link of the chain.

ErrorBody.description: A JSON error: a stable `code` and a message for people.

error_id.description:
`err_` and a ULID, unique to this answer: logged with it (and, for a refused write,
audited as `api.refused`), for the app's "Copy error".

server_time.description: The server's clock in unix seconds, on a `clock_skew` refusal only (handshake spec §5.3).

Event.description:
One entry of the event stream. `seq` only grows: it is the replay cursor, counted gap-free over
the events this device's scopes may see (`x-event-scopes`), so it differs between devices
with different scopes. New kinds may be added: a client skips an event whose kind it does not
know.

kind.description:
What happened: `audit` (an audited change; the payload is the audit row: `audit_seq`,
`action`, `actor_kind`, `actor_id`, `entity_kind`, `entity_id`, `entity_ref`, `details`;
a device is named by its `d_…` id in `entity_ref`, with `entity_id` null), or a kind a
module writes. The registered kinds are listed in `x-event-kinds`. The payload of
`agent.state` is `{session, state, reason, …}`: a live session that finished its answer is
`state: "waiting"` with `reason: "turn_ended"` (its transcript has the harness's
`turn_ended` and a `waiting` entry), and `state: "running"` with `reason: "message"` when
the next message starts an answer. A chain session that waits for an account
says `reason: "waiting"` and `waiting: {until, why, since}` (`until` an RFC 3339 time, `since`
the first wait in unix seconds), and one whose launch refused its account, so another was
picked across a provider or harness, says `reason: "repicked"`, and a run a failover moved across
them says `reason: "failover"`, both with `from` and `to` (each `{provider, harness}`). `account.limited` is `{account, class, until, source}`: an account
cooled or limited until `until` (`class` `rate_limited`, `quota` or `plan_limit`; `source`
`gateway` or `harness`). `account.health` is `{account, user, state, reason}`: an account went
`unhealthy` (`reason` `upstream_errors` or `auth_suspected`). `account.failover` is `{run,
user, from_session, to_session, from_account, to_account, from_pool, to_pool, class, hop}`: a
run moved to `to_session`, or ended (`to_session` null: its chain has nothing left, the hop cap
or the storm guard; `to_account` is null while the successor waits for one). `account.budget` is
`{subject_kind, subject, state}` for an account's or a pool's budget (`state` `warning` or
`exhausted`). `account.expired` is `{account, user, reason}`: a key the provider refused was
confirmed and the account disabled. `alarm.raised` with `alarm` `failover_storm` and a
`user` says the bound on that user's failovers stopped a run of theirs from moving (once per
window and user). `connection.health` is `{connection, user, kind, state, reason}`: a connection's
health changed (`state` `active`, `cooling`, `limited`, `unhealthy` or `disabled`; `reason` a fixed
code: `rate_limited`, `quota`, `upstream_errors`, `auth_suspected`, `auth_failed`, `recovered`,
`auth_cleared`). It is visible to `admin` devices only (`x-event-scopes`), never to a `read` device;
the push for it goes to the owning user's admin devices only. No payload holds a key, a token or an
upstream's own words.

EventActor.description: Who acted, on an audited change.

ExportedSecret.description: One secret of an export. No `Debug`.

owners.description: This page's repos grouped by owner; owners and repos by name.

Handshake.description: What the server is and speaks, for anyone.

api_minor.description: The contract minor this server speaks (`GET /api/v1/me` has it too).

git_sha.description: The commit it was built from (short sha), when the build knew it.

identity_fingerprint.description:
`core_fp`: base64url SHA-256 of the Core identity key's SPKI, 43 characters. Signed
into every request (handshake spec §5.2).

supported_minors.description:
Every minor a client may have been built against and still be served: 0 up to
`api_minor`.

HandshakeBody.description: A liveness proof request: a fresh nonce from the client.

nonce.description: 16 random bytes, base64url without padding (22 characters).

HandshakeProof.description:
`POST /handshake`'s answer: `GET`'s fields plus the proof, which is always present (review
L4). A client that pinned `core_fp` aborts with `core_identity_mismatch` when either is
missing or fails, and never falls back to `GET /handshake` (spec §13).

core_sig.description:
The Core identity key's ES256 signature (raw r||s, base64url) over the UTF-8 string
`AINKRAD-CORE-V1` LF `<host>` LF `<nonce>`, no trailing newline; `host` is the Core's
configured Host (the `Host` it requires), `nonce` the text the client sent.

core_spki.description:
The Core identity key, a P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, base64url. Its fingerprint is
`identity_fingerprint`.

identity_fingerprint.description: `core_fp`, as in `GET /handshake`; a client checks `fp(core_spki)`, not this claim.

paused_until.description: Paused on the Core until then; absent: not paused.

HardwareDecisions.description: Whether Decisions can route heavy jobs.

status.description:

where they were typed); `disabled` (`decisions.heavy_job.enabled` is 0).

decisions.description: Smart job routing (the Decisions service) for commands no rule or history knows.

load_pct.description: Running jobs over all online job slots, 0 to 100.

cmd.description: Run inside the container, one line of 1-512 characters; exit 0 is healthy.

HostBinary.description: A program installed on the host, as the helper's manifest and checks say.

sha256_12.description: The first 12 hex characters of the file's SHA-256.

bin_dir_safe.description: `/usr/local/bin` is root-owned and not group or other writable.

report.description:
Report the local run's outcome and duration (`POST /runner/jobs/report`, the shim's `done`
frame), for the command history.

Which step of the decision made the command heavy.

KindAuthMethod.description: One way to sign in to a kind, easiest first.

advanced.description: Shown under "Advanced", not as the first choice.

available.description:
`false` while the Core lacks what the method needs (Ainkrad's app is not set up yet, an
admin enters it with `setConnectionApp`): the screen says "not set up yet".

result.description:
The status class the provider answered: `ok`, `rate_limited`, `quota`, `auth_failed`,
`server_error`, `unreachable`, `refused_address`, `tls_failed`, `inconclusive` (see

records.description: Records in the room, any status. 0 while nothing was distilled: the items are only imported.

floor.description:
The retention floor: events up to it were trimmed, so a client whose last read seq is
below it re-syncs (E1-04.4). Absent from servers before API minor 2.

type.description: `source`: an imported item, not a distilled record.

total_cost_usd_micros.description: What the distils of this run cost so far, in millionths of a dollar.

unpriced.description: Sessions of the run with no price yet (their cost is not in the total).

provider.description: The provider of the account that did the latest distil, once one ran.

read.description: Sources read by finished distils so far.

sources.description: Sources the run stored in the room.

state.description: `pending`, `learning`, `waiting` (needs an account or a runner) or `done`.

LeaseGrant.description:
A granted lease: hand `lease` to the runner, which redeems it once before `expires_at`.
No `Debug` (review L4): a log line must never print a live lease.

lease.description: `l_…`; only its runner can redeem it.

LeasedSecret.description: A redeemed secret, for the runner only. No `Debug`.

expires_at.description: Drop it by then, or at the session's end.

kind.description:
`text`, `multiline`, `file` (the value is base64: decode it, write it as `file_name`
with `file_mode`) or `env_bundle` (the value is `NAME=value` lines).

room.description: An existing room that no other project is linked to.

LocalTerminalGrant.description: What the app needs to reach the host: present `grant` on `socket`.

lease_secs.description: Seconds one authentication keeps the local connection open. Ask again before then.

Lockout.description: A key that is locked now.

strikes.description: Locks in a row; each doubles the next.

LogLine.description: A page of a service's log, redacted by the helper, newest entries at the end.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next older page; absent on the last.

LoginCode.description: The approval code the user pasted. No `Debug`: it is a one-time secret.

code.description: 8 to 512 of letters, digits and `-_.~#:+/=`; passed to the runner and dropped.

LoginInputBody.description: One line the user typed into a guided sign-in. No `Debug`: it may be a pasted code.

text.description: Up to 512 printable characters, sent to the runner with Enter and dropped.

code.description: The device code, once it printed one.

lines.description: The last lines the sign-in's CLI printed.

url.description: The sign-in page, once it printed one (https on the provider's own hosts).

Me.description: The calling device and what the server speaks.

MergeHint.description: Two rooms that look like one topic; `from` is the smaller. To accept: merge `from` into `to`.

from.description: A proposal id, or the `name` of a suggested room.

into.description: The proposal id to merge into.

reason.description: `prefix` (one name starts the other) or `close` (a spelling within two edits).

MirrorState.description: The Core's copy of a repo.

error.description: Why the last fetch failed; the older head is kept.

head.description: The commit the last fetch ended at.

reason.description:
Why the last fetch failed: `needs_github`, `not_found_or_private`, `auth_failed`,
`timeout`, `ssh_not_supported` or `other`. `error` is the same in one plain sentence.

input_per_mtok_micro.description: List price per million input tokens, in millionths of a dollar.

Named.description: A device: who, by id and name.

rooms.description: How many rooms wait for it.

content_type.description: Its media type, as the client knows it (`image/png`); kept, never interpreted.

data.description: The file, standard base64: 1 byte to 10 MiB once decoded.

name.description:
The file's name as the user knows it: 1 to 255 bytes, no `/`, `\` or control character,
not `.` or `..`. The runner writes it as `<id>-<name>` with anything outside
`[A-Za-z0-9._-]` made `_`.

NewAgentSession.description: A session to start. No `Debug`: the prompt is the caller's.

agent.description:
An opaque agent id (1 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`): its bound chain, else the user's
default chain, serves the session. Needs `admin`. With no chain either way the session
runs as a plain one and names its harness.

chain.description:
A fallback chain's id: the session draws its account from it, one at a time. Needs
`admin`. It must not come with a harness, a model or an `acct.*` secret.

connection_access.description:
Capability names the session may call through its connections (`read_repo`,
`issues_write`, `read_issues`, ...; see `listConnectionKinds`). Needs `admin`. Absent: the
default, read-class capabilities only (write is an explicit grant); an agent's session
with none has no connection tools. An empty list is refused (400 `empty_allowlist`), and
so are operation names and `*` (400).

effort.description:
How hard the harness thinks: `low`, `medium`, `high` or `max`. Claude (its `--effort`) and
Codex (`model_reasoning_effort`) take it; 400 `effort_unsupported` for another harness, 409
`unsupported_command` for a runner too old for it. Absent: the harness's own default.

harness.description:
`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `agy` (what the runner's `agent` driver takes). Omit it
(and `model`) when the session draws from a chain: the account the allocator picks sets them.

live.description:
One live conversation (default `true`): the harness stays up after each answer, the state
is `waiting` until the next `sendAgentMessage`, and the session ends only on `cancel`,
`kill`, the idle end (`agents.idle_end_secs`) or when the CLI exits by itself. `false`, or
a runner that does not offer it (the answer's `live` says), runs one answer and ends.

model.description:
The model id as the provider names it. For a session served by the auth gateway it must be
one of the ids priced for its provider, exactly: the gateway resolves no alias.

plan.description:
Start in Plan mode: the harness reads and plans and edits nothing until the mode is
switched (`setAgentSessionMode`). Only `claude` has one (400 `plan_unsupported`); a
runner too old for it answers 409 `unsupported_command`. Default `false`.

project_id.description:
Start the session for a project (P3-02): the Core builds the workspace from the project's
repos (the primary one first, each under its repo name when there are several), the
runner clones them from the Core's copies, and the project's Brain room, if it has one,
is claimed (the room's model policy then applies, so a session with no chain is refused
403 `claim_refused`). Excludes `workspace` (400). 404 for no such project, 409
`project_archived`, 409 `project_has_no_repos`, 400 when the caller names a mirror in
`workspace`: only the Core sets one.

prompt.description:
The first message. Absent or empty: the session starts with no message, like opening the
CLI: its harness is up, the state is `waiting`, and the first message comes through
`sendAgentMessage`. A message gives the session its `title` (its first 60 characters).

runner.description:
Deprecated and ignored (E15): the Core places every session (on itself, or on a runner
when it is full). Kept so an older client still parses. The one exception: a session of a
runner-bound login (`codex` or `agy` using the login its runner reports, with no account)
stays on the runner it names.

secrets.description: At most 16. Each is leased to the runner at each start (secrets broker, gate G-SEC).

workspace.description:
The repo and worktree to work in (`{"repo_url", "base_branch", "branch", …}`); absent, a
scratch dir.

NewChain.description: A chain to write: `[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}` and 1 to 16 entries. For an edit this replaces the name and the whole list.

NewChainEntry.description: An entry to write: a pool and the model its accounts run.

model.description: A valid model id; an API-key pool's must be priced. Absent, the harness's default.

pool.description:
The pool's id; it must be the caller's user's, of a `claude`, `codex` or `agy` provider,
and in the chain once.

NewConnection.description:
A connection to make with a pasted credential (the Advanced way) or a GitHub App
installation. No `Debug`.

email.description: Jira token: the Atlassian account email.

installation_id.description: `app_install`: the GitHub App installation id the setup page returned.

label.description: What people see, 1 to 80 characters; absent, the kind's title.

token.description: The token or API token; written, never read back.

NewConnectionCredential.description: A replacement credential; the same fields as [`NewConnection`]'s. No `Debug`.

repos.description: 1-10 repos as `owner/name`; the first is primary.

slug.description:
Default: made from the name; a taken or reserved one gets `-2`, `-3`, ... An explicit slug
that is taken is 409 `conflict`.

ttl_secs.description: Each lease's lifetime; default and most `secrets.lease_secs`.

kind.description:
`device` (the default) or `runner`: a runner invite is single use, lasts 15 minutes, is
active at the claim with the `runner` scope, and needs no check code.

name.description: What to call the device that claims it.

scopes.description:
What it may do: within the creator's own scopes. A `runner` invite gets exactly `runner`
(this may be left out).

cwd_rel.description: A wire path relative to the project or session folder; empty is its root.

tty.description: The caller is a terminal: an interactive command answers 409 `interactive`.

runner.description: The runner's device id, `d_…`; it must be in the secret's scope.

provider.description:
A subscription provider: `claude-sub` (a pasted approval code), or the runner-bound
`codex-sub` (a device code; the login stays on that runner and no token comes back).

runner.description:
A runner device id; absent, the best ready runner that has the provider's harness. A
runner-bound provider keeps the login on the runner it runs on: the account is pinned to it.

NewOrder.description: A whole order to write: 1 to 16 accounts, none twice.

NewOrderItem.description: An account to write into an order.

model.description: A valid model id; an API-key account's must be priced. Absent, the harness's default.

kind.description: `device`, `runner`, or `passkey` (a browser, E1-08; only when the Core has passkeys).

name.description: What to call the new device.

scopes.description: What it may do: within the approver's own scopes; a runner gets exactly `runner`.

slug.description: See `ProjectInfo.slug`; it is the project's public host name.

name.description: The folder name: 1-100 of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, not starting with `.` or `-`.

primary.description: Make it the primary repo (the first repo always is).

remote_url.description: An `https://`, `ssh://` or scp-style remote with no credential in it.

chain.description: An existing chain to put the pool in; default: the user's default chain (made if missing).

monthly_limit_usd_micros.description: The monthly dollar limit in micro-dollars; default 20000000 ($20); 0 is no limit.

pool.description: An existing pool of the provider to join; default: the provider's default pool (made if missing).

position.description: 0-based seat of the pool in the chain; default: last.

runners.description: Runner device ids it may be leased to; default none.

value.description: The API key; written, never read back.

file_mode.description: Kind `file`: an octal mode the owner can read, `0400` to `0777`; default `0600`.

group.description: The name of a group made with `createSecretGroup`; one level.

runners.description: Runner device ids it may be leased to; default none (a group's runners then apply).

value.description:
UTF-8 text, at most `secrets.max_bytes`; for kind `file` the file's bytes in standard
base64 (at most 1 MiB decoded); written, never read back.

description.description: One line, at most 200 characters; default empty.

runners.description: Active runner device ids; default none.

cwd.description: An absolute directory to start in; absent, the home folder. Not with `session`.

project.description:
With `sandbox: real` only: start the shell in this project's folder (a cwd on the runner,
not a mount). A sandbox names its project in `sandbox` (400 otherwise).

sandbox.description:
Where the shell lives (D-17): `home` (the default: a private root with the caller's
persistent sandbox home), `project:<id>` or `session:<id>` (that, plus the project's or
session's folder, which the Core resolves: no `cwd`), or `real` (the runner's host view,
allowed only to the Mac that owns a macOS runner, over that Mac's own device key). 400
`bad_request` for a bad value or a `cwd` with a private mode, 403 `real_terminal_refused`
for `real` from anyone else. 409 `runner_update_required` ("Update this runner to open
terminals") when the runner predates sandboxes: no terminal opens on it.

session.description:
Start in the folder of this AI session (`as_…`, its `AgentSession.folder`) without naming
the path: the Core resolves it. The session must be on `runner`, one the caller can see (and
the caller needs the `agent` scope), and its runner must have reported its folder. Not with
`cwd`.

OpsHistory.description: The Core's readings, oldest first, one a minute. Kept in memory: a restart empties it.

OpsSample.description: One minute of the Core's readings.

cpu_pct.description: The Core process's CPU, as a percent of one core; absent for the first sample after a start.

disk_used_bytes.description: The data disk in use and in total, in bytes.

disk_used_pct.description: Share of the data disk in use, 0 to 100.

host_cpu_pct.description: The whole host's CPU, 0 to 100 (a Linux Core only).

memory_bytes.description: The Core process's resident memory in bytes.

ram_used_bytes.description: The host's memory in use and in total, in bytes (a Linux Core only).

model.description: The model to run; absent, the harness's default.

detail.description: Why it waits, failed, or cannot be written.

instructions.description: The editable instructions; approved when `instructions_approved_at` is set.

model.description: The provider and account that wrote it.

picked.description: How many items the local model chose, once known.

source_titles.description: Title of every item a rule cites, by item id (for "from N items").

stage.description:
While `state` is `writing`: `queued` (waiting for its turn), `waiting_runner` (no runner with a
sandbox online), `picking` (the local model is choosing items), `starting` (AI session created,
not running yet), `writing` (AI session running), `reading` (session ended, answer being
read and checked) or `retrying` (first answer rejected, second try queued). Otherwise null.

stage_since.description: When the current `stage` began, RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds.

Page_Event.description: A page of a list. `next_after` is the cursor of the next page, absent on the last.

code.description: The typed code, `ABCDE-FGHJK`: shown once, good once, for 5 minutes.

qr.description: `ainkrad-pair:v1?h=…&p=…&c=<core_fp>&s=<secret>&e=…`, for a QR code: shown once.

PairingView.description: A pairing as the approver sees it.

key_storage.description: Where the claimant says its key lives: a claim, not verified.

sas.description:
The SAS the Core computed from its key and the claimant's: compare it with the new
device's screen, then send it back to approve.

code.description: The same code as for the options; or `secret`.

credential.description:
The created credential as a WebAuthn `RegisterPublicKeyCredential` (`id`, `rawId`,
`type`, `response.attestationObject`, `response.clientDataJSON`, optional
`response.transports`), binary fields base64url.

code.description: The typed code (`ABCDE-FGHJK`, any case); or `secret`.

expires_at.description: The pairing's expiry: the credential must be claimed before it.

options.description:
`{"publicKey": PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions}` (WebAuthn, binary fields base64url):
ES256 only, attestation `none`, user verification required, a resident key preferred.
Decode it and pass it to `navigator.credentials.create`.

PastRetention.description: The 410 of a replay from below the retention floor (E1-04.4).

floor.description: The newest trimmed seq: every event above it is still there.

auto_accept.description: Record types to accept without a review: any of `decision`, `fact`, `preference`, `rule`, `project-state`, `task`, `summary`. An empty list turns it off.

daily_distils.description: Automatic distils a day: 0 turns auto-distil off for the room, the most is 50. A person only (an AI session is refused); no step-up, it only bounds cost.

min_sources.description: 1 to 20: the fewest sources an auto-accepted candidate must cite.

retention_days.description: Compaction is permanent. 1 to 3650 turns it on (step-up; a person only); 0 turns it off (keep). Check `GET /rooms/{room}/retention` first for what it would compact.

PolicyResult.description: The answer to a policy change.

policy.description: The policy now saved on the runner.

restarting.description:
The runner is restarting to apply it: it is offline for a few seconds and then reports the
new policy in `GET /runners` (`policy`). False when nothing it runs changed.

accounts.description: The accounts the room's model policy lets distillation use (none for a local-only room).

auto_accept.description: Candidate kinds accepted without a review; empty (off) by default.

daily_distils.description: Automatic distils a day for the room: 0 is off, the most is 50 (default 12).

local_models.description: Local models a runner declares (none are declared yet).

min_sources.description: An auto-accepted candidate must cite at least this many sources (1 to 20; default 1).

retention_days.description: Sources older than this many days that are fully distilled lose their text and keep a citation stub. Null (the default) keeps everything.

is_default.description: The provider's default pool serves an agent bound to none.

expose.description: Give it a public URL (when the project is exposed); at most one per service.

port.description: The container port, 1-65535. It is only ever published on the runner's loopback.

PriceBookEntry.description: A price: millionths of a dollar per million tokens, and when the provider's list price was read.

items.description: The whole profile: up to 16 answers. A question missing here is retired.

body.description: The answer as one plain sentence, 1 to 200 characters.

removed.description: Earlier answers retired because this `PUT` left them out.

room.description: The personal room the answers went to.

total.description: Rooms in the current write-all (or the one room), and how many are finished.

by_author.description: Commit authors and session titles (`AI sessions` when untitled), by count, most first.

ProjectDefaults.description: What a run gets unless a project says otherwise: the Settings page's Projects > Options.

cpu_limit.description: CPUs a run may use; 2 until set.

idle_minutes.description: Idle stop in minutes; 30 until set.

idle_never.description: Whether the idle stop is off.

mem_limit_mb.description: Memory a run may use in MB; 4096 until set.

default_environment.description: The run environment a Run button uses by default; one of the project's.

expose.description: Whether the running project gets a public link.

fetch_interval_minutes.description: Minutes between automatic fetches: 10, 15, 60, or 0 for only when asked.

idle_never.description: The idle stop is off: the run keeps going while nobody visits.

repos.description: The primary repo first, then by name.

room.description: The linked Brain room; null when the Brain is off or the project has none.

runner.description: Where it prefers to run: `auto`, `this_mac` or `home_server`.

slug.description: A DNS label, 2-40 of `a-z0-9-`, starting with a letter; not a reserved name.

mirror.description: None until the Core has tried to fetch it.

name.description: The folder name in a multi-repo checkout.

remote_url.description: The source of truth; never carries a credential.

ProjectRoom.description: The Brain room linked to a project (strictly 1:1).

config_id.description: The run configuration it started from, when it did (Core 0.10).

error.description: What went wrong, for a failed run (redacted).

idle_stop_at.description: When the idle stop is due, for a running run.

job.description:
A `task` configuration's heavy job (`j_…`, E15-3): follow it with `/jobs/{id}`. Absent for a
service run.

runner.description: The runner it is placed on.

stop_reason.description:
Why it ended, or is ending: `user`, `idle`, `crash`, `runner_lost`, `replaced` or
`start_failed`.

ProjectSecretInfo.description: A project secret, never its value.

last_used_at.description: When a runner last redeemed it; none before the first redemption.

version.description: 1 when stored, one more per rotation.

by_day.description: Cost per day, last 7 days, oldest first, USD micros.

sessions.description: The project's sessions, newest first (at most 30).

sessions_week.description: Sessions started in the last 7 days.

week_cost.description: Cost of the last 7 days in USD micros (millionths), as the cost ledger stores it.

semantic.description:
The local model's sorting step for this run: `pending`, `ready` or `off` (only in the
proposals list; the suggestions are at `/imports/{run}/semantic`).

suggest_merge.description: A room this one looks like (only in the proposals list); merging is the user's call.

replaces.description:
A memory record this one disagrees with. An AI may not contest memory: a proposal that sets
it is dropped (`contests_memory`).

sources.description:
Item ids of sources this session read through `brainAiEvidence` (at most 20). A proposal
that cites none is dropped.

tags.description: At most 8 tags of 1 to 40 characters.

type.description:
`fact` or `summary`; a `decision` is saved only when a user turn says it. `task` and
`project-state` are dropped for now. Never `rule` or `preference`.

duplicate.description: True when memory already held the statement (`status` is `reinforced`).

id.description: The new record's id when `status` is `saved`; empty otherwise.

reason.description: The first reason code of a drop.

status.description:
`saved` (in memory, with Undo for the person), `reinforced` (memory already held it) or
`dropped` (it did not pass the checks; nothing is queued).

Provider.description: A provider definition: a built-in, or user data validated before it is stored.

key_prefix.description:
The shape this provider's keys start with (6 to 16 characters, never a built-in's, such
as `sk-or-v1-`). A definition that sets it holds keys, and then only through the gateway
(`delivery` is `["gateway"]`): the broker binds each key to the account's host by it.

models.description:
Model ids exactly as the provider names them: the gateway compares a request's model with
the ids it was granted, as they are, and resolves no alias (`-latest`). `:online` is refused.

preset.description:
A preset provider (OpenRouter, Groq, ...): shipped in code, read-only, the user only
pastes a key. Its keys are bound to the account and its frozen host, not to a prefix.

priced_at.description: When the models' list prices were read.

test_path.description:
The authenticated path (under the base URL, such as `/key`) of the one-shot account test,
for a provider whose model list needs no key (OpenRouter's is public: a revoked key would
read as `ok`). A user definition without one cannot be tested: the answer is
`inconclusive`. Built-ins use their wire's own model list.

wire.description:
The API dialect the gateway speaks to this provider: `anthropic-messages` (claude),
`openai-responses` (codex) or `gemini-generate` (agy). Optional on write: it is its
harness's own, and any other is refused.

ProviderAccount.description:
An account as a `read` device sees it: its key's last four characters, never the key, the
broker secret's name or the runners it may be leased to.

base_url.description: The provider's base URL when the account was stored.

cap.description: Sessions that may hold the account at once; 0 is no cap.

health.description:
What the scheduler keeps of its health. Only the reads say it; `state`, `state_reason`
and `state_until` (a cooldown's end) are above.

last_test.description: The last one-shot test of the key; absent when it was never tested.

live.description:
Sessions that hold a slot of its cap now (`starting`, `running`, `interrupted`). Only the
reads (`listAccounts`, `getAccount`) say it.

masked_tail.description: The key's last four characters; empty for a key too short to show any.

models_enforced.description:
Whether a model the person switched off for this account is refused in its sessions: true for
an API-key account (its gateway grants only the models left on), false for a subscription or
runner-bound login, where the harness talks to its provider itself and the Core only skips the
account when a session asks for a switched-off model at its start. The app shows the
limit as advice when it is false.

month_limit_usd_micros.description: The account's monthly dollar budget cap, when one is set; absent when it has none.

month_spend_usd_micros.description:
What the account cost this calendar month (UTC), in millionths of a US dollar, from the
cost ledger. Only the reads say it, and only to an `admin` device.

runner.description:
The runner device a runner-bound subscription (Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity) signed in on:
its sessions run only there. Absent for any other account. An `admin` device only; a device
id is not a secret.

session_limits.description: What one session may spend through this account; absent when only the budgets limit it.

usage.description:
The row's usage meter: how much of its plan or budget is used and whether it can take work
now. Only the reads say it, and only to an `admin` device.

wipe_note.description:
A plain-language limit of removing this account, e.g. an Antigravity login that stays in the
runner's keyring. Absent when removal clears everything.

PushKinds.description: The notification kinds the calling device is pushed (E2-12.3).

kinds.description:
The kinds it opted into, e.g. `approval_needed`; `null` is every kind its scopes allow
(the default). A kind needs its scope on top: a `read` device is never sent an approval.

sandbox.description: A development build's token, for the sandbox gateway.

token.description: The device token, hex, as the app got it from APNs.

period_key.description: The period that ran out: `2026-10-22`, a week's Monday, `2026-10` or `total`.

tokens.description: Tokens to add (0 when raising dollars).

usd_micros.description: Millionths of a dollar to add.

RedeemLease.description: A lease to redeem. No `Debug` (review L4).

change.description: The change set to Undo (`POST /rooms/{room}/changes/{id}/undo`); none for a dry run.

dry_run.description: A dry run reads and counts, and writes no memory.

kept.description: Facts that stay (re-derived, or protected), facts written, and old facts archived. Set when `done`.

state.description:
`running`, `committing`, `done`, `failed` (start it again within 24 hours to resume) or
`cancelled`.

summary.description: "Kept 84 facts, archived 1,203 items" (a dry run: "Would keep ..."). Set when `done`.

total.description: Sources the run reads, and how many it has read.

dropped.description: Earlier proposals whose key is gone (merged away, split off or no longer produced).

kept.description: Proposals that kept the user's decisions (name, kind, config, state).

name.description: 1 to 64 characters, no control characters; trimmed.

ReplaceKey.description: A replacement key, and optionally a new runner scope. No `Debug`.

ahead.description: Commits that branch has beyond the default branch.

behind.description: Commits the default branch has beyond that branch.

branch.description: The most recently updated branch (the default one when it is the only one).

files.description: Files in the branch shown; 0 before the first fetch.

last_commit.description: The branch's newest commit; null before the first fetch.

request_id.description: The id the restart is audited under (`host.restart_requested`, `host.action_result`).

restored.description: False when it was not archived.

chars.description: Characters of text that would be dropped.

would_compact.description: Sources that would lose their text if retention were set to `days` now.

RevealedSecret.description: A secret's value, shown to the person who asked. No `Debug`.

project.description: Project keys (a repo folder, a workspace name or a Citadel key) that may see the room.

runner.description: Runner ids whose AI sessions may see the room.

session.description: AI session ids that may see the room.

RoomAlias.description:
One "same project as" answer: rooms named `from` (normalized: lowercase letters and digits)
are filed as `to`.

readers.description: Device ids that may read the room besides an admin (an admin sees every room, Q-14).

RoomHint.description: A topic found among the Unsorted items. To accept: split Unsorted with these `item_ids` and `name`.

created.description: False when the room already existed (a resumed commit or a later run).

sources.description: Sources written to the room by this commit.

open.description: Whether the room's lease is live.

sources.description: Sources stored, counted from hashes in the control plane (no need to open the room).

RotateSecret.description: A rotation: the new value, and optionally a new scope or delivery. No `Debug`.

group.description: An empty string leaves the group.

kind.description: Omitted keeps the kind; the other fields are those of `createSecret`, omitted keeps them.

sources.description: Item ids of the room's items it came from; all were shown to the model.

kind.description:
`service` (a container that keeps running) or `task` (runs as a heavy job on the hardware
`place_job` picks, with the environment's variables as leased env). Absent: `service`.

restart.description:
Come back after a crash: the Core restarts it after 2 s, 4 s, ... up to 60 s, at most 5
times in 10 minutes, then gives up (event `project.run_gave_up`). A run a person stopped
does not restart.

runner.description: `automatic`, or the id of a runner.

service.description:
The service of the run spec it is laid over; none lets the Core pick (the first that
mounts a repo).

workdir.description: A folder in the service's repo checkout (`./app`), or an absolute path in the container.

environment.description: The environment to run in; default the project's first.

replace.description:
Stop this configuration's live run first (other configurations keep running); default
false.

environments.description: In order; the first is the default. A new project has `Development` and `Staging`.

seq.description: Grows by one per line of the run; pass the last one as `after` to continue.

RunLogs.description: A page of lines; the WebSocket sends one per poll (only when it has lines or a gap).

lost.description: Lines before the first one that the runner had already dropped (a flood, or a slow reader).

run.description: The live run these belong to; none (and no services) when the project is not running.

RunSpec.description: The whole spec: its services by name.

services.description:
1-16 services. A name is 1-20 of `a-z0-9-`, starting with a letter: it is the service's
network alias and part of its public host name.

file.description: The file it was drafted from, as a path inside the repo.

repo.description: The repo it was read from.

version.description: The draft, saved as the project's next spec version; its `origin` names the converter.
1 for the first save, then one more each time.

secret.description: For `secret`: the project secret it comes from. Its value is never returned.

size.description:
For `plain`: the value's length in bytes (a client may draw dots); the value itself comes
from the reveal route only.

Runner.description: A paired runner and its live state.

accounts.description: Whether it can serve the accounts' kinds of key, with the reason when it cannot.

arch.description: The CPU architecture it reported (`aarch64`, `x86_64`), once connected.

built_in.description: The runner `runner-enroll-local` made on the Core's own machine (the installer's).

connected_since.description: When its current connection began; absent when it is offline.

degraded.description: Connected but silent past two heartbeats.

drivers.description: What it last advertised (empty until it first connected since the Core started).

home.description: The folder its work happens in, as the runner reports it.

host_load.description: The host's load as its runner last reported it (E2-15.2), if it has.

isolation.description:
The isolation it offers now (E8a-09): absent until it reports, and then no tier can be
assumed.

last_error.description: Why it is not fully working, in words: its last-error note.

last_seen.description: Its last frame or request; null if never seen.

os_pretty.description: The system as a person names it, `Ubuntu 26.04`, as the runner reported it.

own_logins.description:
Harnesses with a login of their own on its host (`claude`, `codex`, ...); a plain session
of one is not refused as `no_account`. Absent until a runner of this version connected.

policy.description:
What the runner offers now: terminals, agents, agent capacity (`PUT /runners/{id}/policy`
sets it). Absent until a runner of this version connected.

runs_as.description: The user the runner process runs as, and whether that is root.

sandbox.description:
`process` when the runner offers a process sandbox for agents, else `none`; absent when it
did not report (agents off).

slots.description: Sessions and terminals running now, and how many it takes.

tool_install.description:
The AI tool install under way on its host, or the last one, as the runner reports it in
its heartbeats (D-22). Absent until a runner of this version reports.

tools.description:
Tools it found on its host, name to version (`claude` to `2.1.318`, `git`, `node`, `python`,
`go`, `rust`, `docker`, `codex`); a tool that is not installed is not listed.

update_available.description: This Core's own version is newer than the runner's `version`. Absent until it connected.

update_required.description:
E12-5: the runner is older than the oldest this Core works with (`GET /core/health` `min_runner`), so the app asks
to update it before relying on it. Absent until it connected.

updating.description: E12-4: asked to update in the last 15 minutes (it restarts and reconnects on the new version). Absent when not.

RunnerAccounts.description: What a runner can do for accounts: each answer, and why not when it is `false`.

egress_filter.description: Sessions' network is filtered by an allow list.

gateway.description: API-key accounts through the auth gateway.

subscription_env.description:
A subscription's token handed to a session as an environment variable (needs the sandbox
and a proven egress filter).

RunnerDriver.description: A driver a runner offers, as it advertised it.

capacity.description: How many of its commands run at once (`agent`: sessions).

slots.description: `agent`: how many sessions each harness may run at once (E2-08.1); absent, no split.

RunnerHostLoad.description: The host's load as last reported by a runner (E2-15.2), if any.

cores.description: How many CPUs the runner sees.

RunnerIsolation.description: The isolation tiers a runner offers and the state of its `/dev/kvm` (E8a-09).

RunnerJobReport.description: `POST /runner/jobs/report`: a local run the Core said to report (`JobLocal.report`).

RunnerNewJob.description:
`POST /runner/jobs`: what the built-in runner forwards from a shim, with the origin it stamped
(the sandbox the socket belongs to, never the shim's word).

cwd_rel.description: A wire path relative to the session or project folder (the runner maps the shim's `cwd`).

hosts.description:
A `filtered` sandbox's allowed host names; a job sent elsewhere gets them cut to the
registry list.

network.description:
The sandbox's own network: `allow`, `deny` or `filtered` (E15 H2). Absent or unknown is
`deny`: the command runs where it was typed.

session.description: The AI session (`as_…`) whose sandbox the shim ran in.

terminal.description: The Core terminal it ran in.

history_offered.description: The runner was started with `--share-history`, so it can answer a history read.

tools.description: The harness tools the runner offers for AI sessions (`claude`, `codex`, ...).

RunnerPolicyBody.description: What a runner offers: terminals, agents, and how many agent sessions at once.

agent_capacity.description: How many agent sessions run at once, 1 to 8.

agents.description:
Agent sessions are offered. Refused (409 `policy_refused`, with the reason) when the
runner cannot run them: no process sandbox, no proven egress filter, or no agent tool installed.

runs.description:
The runner takes project runs. Omitted: the runner's current setting stays (off for a
runner that never had one). Runs are placed only on runners with it on.

share_history.description:
The runner lets the Brain read its Claude Code history (`--share-history`). Omitted: the
runner's current setting stays; `false` turns it off.

terminals.description: Terminals are offered on the runner.

RunnerSlots.description: A runner's work, split by kind.

agents_capacity.description: How many agent sessions it takes at once; absent when agents are off or it is unknown.

agents_used.description: Agent sessions starting, running or interrupted on it.

terminals_capacity.description: How many terminals it takes at once; absent when terminals are off or it is unknown.

terminals_used.description: Terminals created or running on it.

RunnerToolInstall.description: An AI tool install as a runner reports it.

description.description: One line: what the group is for.

runners.description: The runner devices its members may be leased to unless they list their own.

delivery.description: How a runner hands it to a session: `env`, `file` or `askpass`.

description.description: One line: what it is for.

effective_runners.description: The runners a lease may go to: its own, else its group's.

file_name.description: A `file` secret's name on the runner, and its octal mode (`0600`).

group.description: The group it belongs to (`/api/v1/secret-groups`); none for no group.

key_id.description: The master key it is sealed under.

kind.description: `text`, `multiline`, `file` or `env_bundle`. `size` is a file's decoded length.

last_used_at.description: When a runner last redeemed it; none before the first redemption.

runners.description: The runner devices it may be leased to (its scope); empty: none.

version.description: 1 when stored, one more per rotation.

SecretsExport.description: Every secret the Secrets screen lists, with its value. No `Debug`.

SemanticProgress.description: Items of this step the local model has read so far, of `total` to read (stored ones count as read).

ai_tidy.description:
When `ready`: what the local model changed by itself in the proposal (duplicates merged,
rooms merged or folded, items moved), with the link to the list of changes. Absent before.

closest.description: Unsorted items that look like they belong in an existing room. Never filed on their own.

progress.description: While `pending`: how far the local model is ("Local AI: 1,240 of 2,980 items"). Absent otherwise.

state.description: `pending` (working now), `ready` or `off` (no local model, or the step failed).

Service.description: One container. Exactly one of `image` and `build`.

build.description: Build the image from a Dockerfile in one of the project's repos.

command.description: Replaces the image's command; at most 64 arguments.

depends_on.description: Services that must be started (and healthy, when they have a `health`) first.

env.description: Environment. A value is plain text or contains `${secret:NAME}` references.

image.description: An image reference such as `postgres:17` or `ghcr.io/acme/app@sha256:...`.

ports.description: At most 8 ports the service listens on.

repo.description: Mount this project repo's checkout at `/repo/<name>`.

volumes.description: Named volumes: volume name to the absolute container path it is mounted at.

workdir.description: Absolute path inside the container; default is the image's.

The browser's session key: a non-extractable WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 key's SPKI
(`exportKey("spki")` of its public half), base64url.

16 random bytes, base64url: offer `ainkrad.v1, ainkrad-ticket.<ticket>` as the
