device_signature.description: ES256 over the canonical request string, with Ainkrad-Device, Ainkrad-Session, Ainkrad-Alg, Ainkrad-Timestamp and Ainkrad-Nonce alongside (handshake spec §5)
device_signature.name: Ainkrad-Signature

info.description: The Ainkrad Core client API, for the Ainkrad app. Every request is signed by the device's own P-256 key (ES256, raw r||s): the headers Ainkrad-Device, Ainkrad-Session, Ainkrad-Alg (ES256), Ainkrad-Timestamp, Ainkrad-Nonce and Ainkrad-Signature cover an exact canonical string of the Core identity fingerprint, the method, path, query, time, nonce and the body's SHA-256 (handshake spec §5). A session comes from POST /handshake/challenge then POST /handshake/session and lasts 15 minutes; there is no bearer secret, and an Authorization header is refused. A signed body is at most 1 MiB: a larger one is answered 401 auth_failed and counted as a failure against the address, so keep uploads below it. Before trusting a Core, POST /handshake with a fresh nonce and check that core_sig verifies under core_spki and that its fingerprint is the pinned one. Requests carry the server's own Host and no Origin, or the Core's own origin from its web client. A web client signs in with a passkey (POST /handshake/passkey/options, then POST /handshake/passkey/session) and signs every request with a non-extractable WebCrypto P-256 session key in the same way; its event socket takes a one-time ticket (POST /api/v1/ws-ticket) in Sec-WebSocket-Protocol. Times are RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds. Versioning: within /api/v1, enum values, union variants, optional fields and operations may be added; a client must keep an unknown enum value (every enum is open) and skip an event or union variant it cannot decode. Anything removed or renamed is a new /api/v2. `info.version` is `1.<minor>.0`; the minor (`GET /api/v1/me`, `versions.api.minor`) is bumped on every addition.
info.title: Ainkrad Core

200.description: Every account: its key's last four characters, never the key, its secret's name or its runner scope; with its `live` session count and `health`, `month_spend_usd_micros`, `month_limit_usd_micros` and `usage` (the usage meter) (`admin` devices only)

Stored with its key in the secrets broker (audited as `account.created`, and the broker's own `secret.created`). 409 `secrets_disabled` (`secrets.mode` 0), `real_secret_refused` (a real key shape while `secrets.provider_accounts` is off), `conflict` or `limit_reached`; 400 for a bad provider, label, cap or runner; 503 `secrets_unavailable`

A sign-in began on a runner (audited as `account.login_started`, event `account.login.started`); poll it for the URL. 409 `no_runner` (none is ready with the harness and sign-in support), `conflict` (the label is taken or open), `secrets_disabled` or `real_secret_refused` (a gate the stored token would meet is closed), `limit_reached`; 400 for a provider with no browser sign-in or a bad label; 503 `secrets_unavailable`. A step-up
Cancelled (audited as `account.login_cancelled`, event `account.login.failed` with the reason `cancelled`) and the runner told to drop it; one that already ended is returned as it is
Its state: never a token or a code. Only the device that started it sees it; 404 otherwise

The code went to the runner (once, never stored or logged); the sign-in is `waiting_code` until the account is stored. 409 `login_state` unless the sign-in is `open_url`; 400 for a code of the wrong shape (never echoed). No step-up beyond the one that started it

One line went to the guided sign-in's terminal on its runner (once, never stored or logged). Only for a provider whose sign-in is guided (`opencode-sub`); 409 `login_state` unless the sign-in is `open_url`; 400 for a line that is not printable text; 409 `runner_failed`. No step-up beyond the one that started it
The redacted screen of a guided sign-in, read from its runner now. Only the device that started it; 409 `login_state` unless `open_url`
The built-in providers, then the user definitions
Stored (audited as `provider.created`). 400 for a definition that fails validation (https DNS base URL, the harness's own variable); 409 `conflict` or `limit_reached`
Deleted (audited as `provider.deleted`); a built-in or one an account uses is refused
A new version (audited as `provider.updated`). Accounts already stored keep the base URL they were bound to

Needs `admin`. Every account's tokens, messages and dollars over the last five hours and seven days, and its recent drops. Events that carry only a `legacy_account_id` (Citadel's old account id) are not counted here until the account port lands

Removed with an Undo window (audited as `account.deleted`): at once it is gone from every list, out of its pool seats and the AI order, takes no new session and holds no lease. `undo_until` is when `POST /accounts/{id}/restore` stops working; after it the key, the row, the seats, the budgets and a runner-bound login on its runner are wiped for good (audited as `account.wiped`)
One account, with its `live` session count and `health` (`admin` devices only)
The concurrency cap, 0 (no cap) to 64 (audited as `account.cap_set`)

Whether the account works. A Claude plan account: the token is leased to a runner that offers `subscription-env` and `plan-check`, which runs `claude -p` with a one-word prompt in its sandbox; it answers `ok` or the reason (`token_expired`, `no_runner`, `egress_not_proven`, ...). It uses a little of the plan's quota, never money. Any other account keeps its key test (`testAccount`'s answer, with `no_runner` as a result). Stored on the account and audited as `account.tested`. 429 when the account was checked within a minute or a check is running

The model ids the provider listed for the account when its key was added or checked (a preset's list is read through a runner's gateway), and in `items` each model with its list price where there is one and whether it is allowed. 404 for no such account

Allows or switches off the model for the account (audited as `account.model_allowed_set`); a chain, the AI order and a gateway grant refuse a switched-off model. Needs a step-up. 404 for no such account
Undoes a delete within its window (audited as `account.restored`): its state and its pool seats come back. 404 for an account that is not removed or whose window has ended
A new key version, its last four characters cut again, every outstanding lease on the old one dropped (audited as `account.secret_replaced`); the refusals of `createAccount`

What one session may spend through this account (audited as `account.session_limits_set`); a dimension left out is cleared. The Core's ceiling for a gateway session honours it beside the budgets, from the next time a ceiling is set (a session's start, its resume, or the top-up of its ceiling): a session that is running keeps the ceiling it holds until then. It raises what a session may spend, so it needs a step-up
Enables (`active`) or disables the account, or marks it cooling, limited or unhealthy (audited as `account.state_set`)

One free request (a model list) made through the gateway of a runner that is online, in the key's scope and offers it: the status class and the latency, never a body. Stored on the account and audited as `account.tested`. 409 `no_runner` when none is ready; 429 when the account was tested within a minute or a test is running. A provider whose model list needs no key and that declares no `test_path` answers `inconclusive` (nothing is sent), never `ok`

Started on the runner (`running`), or `starting` while the runner is away (audited as `agent.created`). 409 `runner_offline` or `unsupported_command` (no agent driver), 503 `runner_busy` (its capacity or the harness's slot is full), the secrets broker's refusals (`secrets_disabled`, `limit_reached`, 400 when the runner is not in a secret's scope). With `chain` or `agent` (admin only, else 403): the session starts with no account and the allocator picks one from the chain (`waiting` while every account cools); 404 for no such chain, 400 for a harness, a model or an `acct.*` secret beside a chain. 409 `no_account` for a plain create of claude, codex or agy that names no `acct.*` secret and no credential variable of its own (it would answer "Not logged in"). A chain create passes a plain create's checks for the harness of every entry, and the runner must be online with room for at least one entry (else its refusal, 409 or 503), all before any row; an entry the runner cannot serve is skipped at the pick
One session
Sets the session's short `title` (at most 60 characters, trimmed; empty clears it; audited as `agent.renamed`)

The Code Mode writes of this session the Core holds for a person's approval now (request ids `cm_…`, decided with `decideAgentApproval`). A harness's own tool approvals are `approval_request` entries of the transcript instead. Newest last

The waiting tool call is allowed or denied, from any device with `approve` (audited as `agent.decided`). 502 `runner_failed` when no such request waits. A request id starting `cm_` is a Code Mode write the Core holds for approval (see `listAgentApprovals`): 404 `not_found` when unknown, 409 `approval_closed` when it was decided, timed out or ended

Kept with the session (audited as `agent.attachment_added`, its id and size only) until the session row goes or the session has been over for 7 days. Name its id in `sendAgentMessage`'s `attachments`: the runner then writes the file into the session's folder (`<folder>/.ainkrad/attachments/<id>-<name>`) and the message ends with its path (`@<path>` for Claude Code). The caller needs the same rights as for a message. 400 `bad_request` (not base64, empty, a bad `content_type`), `bad_attachment_name`; 413 `attachment_too_large` (over 10 MiB), `attachments_full` (the session's attachments would pass 100 MiB); 403 `forbidden_scope` (a session holding secrets, not the caller's); 409 `module_owned`
Its tool call in flight finishes, then it ends (killed after the runner's grace; audited as `agent.cancelled`)

parameters.description: A folder of the session, relative to its folder (no `..`); absent or empty, the folder itself.

200.description: One level of the session's folder on its runner: directories first, then by name, at most 500 (`truncated` says there were more); `.git`, `node_modules` and the like are left out, a symbolic link is listed as a file and never followed. Call again with `dir` for a folder's own entries. Read like the transcript (a session holding secrets answers only to its creator or an admin). 400 `bad_path` (`..`, outside the folder), 409 `session_folder_unknown`, `session_folder_gone`, `unsupported_command` (a runner too old), `runner_offline`

Puts the file back as it was before the session's edits (audited as `agent.file_reverted`, the path and what was done). The session's recorded edits of that file (its `tool_use` entries' `edit`) are reverse-applied on the runner, newest first: no git needed, and only what the session did is undone; a file the session created is deleted (restored from git `HEAD` instead when git tracks it). Edits the record cannot reverse (a cut text, a removal inside the file) fall back to the file's git `HEAD` copy. 409 `revert_conflict` when the file no longer holds the recorded text (nothing is changed), `revert_impossible` (no usable record and git has no copy), `session_folder_unknown`, `session_folder_gone`, `unsupported_command` (a runner too old), `module_owned`; 400 `bad_path`

Writes `content` (at most 256 KiB) to the file `path` of the session's folder on its runner, creating the folders on the way inside it (audited as `agent.file_written`, the path and size, never the text). A symbolic link on the way, `..` or a path outside the folder is refused, and so is anything under `.git`. 400 `bad_path`; 413 `file_too_large`; 409 `session_folder_unknown`, `session_folder_gone`, `unsupported_command` (a runner too old), `module_owned`

Stops the running answer of a live session, like Esc in the CLI (audited as `agent.interrupted`): a tool call waiting for approval is denied, the session goes on and becomes `waiting` (a message queued behind the answer is taken next). Nothing happens while it waits. 409 `not_live` for a session that is not a live conversation, `session_over`; `cancel` ends the session
Its harness is killed now and its delivered secrets removed (audited as `agent.killed`). A module's session: `admin` only, the break-glass stop when the module's own routes cannot

Given to the harness as its next turn (audited as `agent.messaged`, its length only). A live session takes it in its running process: `waiting` becomes `running`, and a message sent while an answer runs is queued behind it. A live session whose process is gone (a runner restart, a lost runner, an idle end) is started again with the harness's own resume in the same folder and gets it there, so the conversation goes on. A first message gives an untitled session its `title`. `attachments` (from `addAgentAttachment`) are written into the session's folder on its runner first, and the message the harness gets ends with their paths, one a line (`@<path>` for Claude Code); a message with attachments may have no text. 400 `unknown_attachment` (not this session's, or swept). 409 `session_over`, `session_starting` (not on its runner yet), `unsupported_command` (a runner too old for attachments), 502 `runner_failed` when it is not running

Sets the session's permission mode (`policy`), Plan mode (`plan`), or both (audited as `agent.mode_changed` with the mode before and after). A session on its runner (`running`, `waiting`) takes it at once: its next tool calls are decided by it, Claude switches live, another harness at its next turn (resumed with the new flags), and its transcript gets a `mode_changed` entry. A session off its runner (`interrupted`, `lost`, `ended`) takes it at its next start. 400 for neither field or an unknown `policy`, 400 `plan_unsupported` for `plan` on a harness other than claude, 409 `mode_at_start` for a switch into `sandboxed` (it decides where a session runs), 409 `session_starting`, `unsupported_command` (a runner too old to switch), `runner_offline`, `module_owned`
A `lost` or `interrupted` session is started again on its runner, continuing the harness's own session, with fresh leases (audited as `agent.resumed`). 409 `not_resumable` otherwise

200.description: Stops that one sub-agent, not the answer (audited as `agent.subagent_stopped`): its harness is told at once, and the tool call ends with its `tool_result` while the answer goes on. `can_stop_subagents` says whether the session can. 404 `unknown_subagent` for an id that is not a sub-agent's call of this session with no result yet. 409 `unsupported_command` for a harness that cannot stop one sub-agent (or a runner too old to relay it), `session_over`, `module_owned`

Queued on the scheduler (audited as `agent.wake_queued`): once the session is idle it is resumed on its runner, continuing the harness's own session with `text` as its next turn (`agent.woken`). A session that is still running is retried for a while, then the wake is dropped (a wake queued for an attempt a failover replaced goes to its run's newest). 409 `failed_over` (the session was replaced: the message names the attempt to wake), 409 `not_wakeable` (failed, cancelled, a module's), 409 `limit_reached` (too many wakes waiting), 503 `scheduler_unavailable`
The caller's user's AI order and per-agent overrides

The agent walks the default order again (audited as `chain.unbound`); 404 when it had no override
The agent's own order; its sessions walk it instead of the default one. The refusals of `setAiOrder`; 400 for a bad agent id
